title: Turning AutoPay Back On After a Returned AutoPay Debit - Credit Builder Accounts
content:
## AutoPay after a returned AutoPay debit

When a borrower whose AutoPay debit (a payment made through the AutoPay channel) was returned turns AutoPay on again for a Credit Builder account, the borrower authorizes the recurring debit from their own linked checking account, and the due day is reset as the Credit Builder Accounts AutoPay re-enrollment policy sets out.

For an account whose AutoPay debit was returned and that turns AutoPay on again, and only for such an account, the due day is reset as that policy sets out to line the debit up with the borrower's funds, even when the account's one due-day change has already been used and without using it up, and a reset that moves the due day makes the first new due date the first date on the new day later than the current next due date, which falls in the same month because the new day is never earlier than the current one; for every other account the due day may be changed once per account, to a day from 1 to 28, with the first new due date the first date on the new day later than the current next due date.

| Account | Due day when AutoPay is turned on |
|---|---|
| an AutoPay debit on it was returned, and AutoPay is turned on again | reset under the re-enrollment policy, without using the one due-day change |
| any other account | may be changed once per account, to a day from 1 to 28 |

A reset that moves the due day from the 10th to the 14th, with a current next due date of 10 July, makes 14 July the first new due date (hypothetical dates).

## The borrower's AutoPay authorization: `reenroll_autopay_5af065e7`

**What it does.** With this tool the borrower turns AutoPay back on for their own Credit Builder account and sets its due day. Turning AutoPay on authorizes recurring monthly debits of the payment from the named linked bank account, and sets the account's due day to the day given and its next due date to the date given. The borrower sees AutoPay on, the due day and the next due date on the account.

**How it is invoked.** It is the borrower's own tool: the agent unlocks `reenroll_autopay_5af065e7` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `builder_account_id` | reference number of the borrower's Credit Builder account, as returned by the Credit Builder account lookup |
| `bank_account_id` | reference number of the borrower's linked checking account the AutoPay debits come from, as returned by the linked bank account lookup |
| `payment_due_day` | the due day of the month the account takes, an integer from 1 to 28 (the current due day when it does not change) |
| `next_due_date` | the account's next due date on that due day, written as YYYY-MM-DD (calendar date, no time zone); the current next due date when the due day does not change |

**Return.** A confirmation of the form "AutoPay on for <account reference> from <bank account reference>; due day <day>, next due date <YYYY-MM-DD>." Receiving this text means AutoPay is enrolled and the due day and next due date are updated.
